title: SensCluster: Sensitivity-Guided Client Clustering for Feature-Skewed Federated Learning

problem.claim: Federated Learning performance degrades under heterogeneous data distributions.

gap.claim: Existing clustered federated learning methods primarily address label distribution skew and overlook feature distribution skew.

contributions.claim: SensCluster is a sensitivity-aware clustered federated learning framework that constructs compact client representations by selecting parameters responsive to local feature distributions.
SensCluster uses Fisher information to retain influential parameters for sensitivity-aware clustering representations while reducing interference from irrelevant features.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly presents SensCluster as a novel sensitivity-aware clustered federated learning framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SensCluster consistently outperforms state-of-the-art clustered federated learning methods across diverse feature skew scenarios on image and time-series benchmarks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning supports collaborative training without sharing raw data but suffers under heterogeneous data distributions.
Clustered federated learning addresses heterogeneity, but existing methods largely overlook feature distribution skew.
Under feature distribution skew, network layers differ substantially in sensitivity, with early layers encoding client-specific feature patterns that affect aggregation.
SensCluster selects parameters responsive to local feature distributions and uses Fisher information to construct sensitivity-aware client representations.
Experiments across image and time-series benchmarks are reported to show consistent gains over state-of-the-art clustered federated learning methods.

source_observation.claim: Different network layers have unequal sensitivity under feature distribution skew, and early layers encode strongly client-specific feature patterns.

interpretation.claim: Selective representation of parameters may reduce aggregation interference caused by feature-skewed clients.

application.claim: Federated learning systems with feature distribution skew could consider sensitivity-aware client representations for clustering.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported feature-skew scenarios and benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact clustering algorithm or sensitivity-selection procedure.
The abstract does not provide quantitative performance results or statistical significance.
The abstract does not describe computational overhead, communication cost, or ablation results.
